extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners / patent office personnel (and practitioners interested in KIPO examination practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Official KIPO examination manual guidance for conducting prior-art searches and substantive examination of patent applications, including processing deadlines, search scope and methods, citation rules, outsourced search handling, and priority/other special-application procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing deadlines for examination and reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications where a request for reexamination is made after a decision to reject or remanded from appeal, the examiner shall begin examination within one month from receipt of application documents; if unable to start within one month for unavoidable reasons, reasons must be reported to supervisory heads. For expedited examination requests, the examiner shall determine whether the application falls under expedited category within 7 days from receipt of the request; examination shall begin within 2 months from delivery of the notice of the examiner’s decision (with certain expedited cases allowed up to 4 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes reference table of other processing timelines (e.g., 15 days, 1 month, 2 months, 3 months, etc.) for actions such as prior-art search request delivery, receipt dates for amendments, examination deferral/resume, divisional applications, and term extension requests. If deadlines cannot be met, report reasons to appropriate supervisory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for application of revised law to pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Patent Act is revised while an application is pending, transitional measures are applied to prevent disadvantages; provisions of law shall be applied as of the filing date. Divisional/converted applications and applications by lawful successors are deemed filed as of the parent application filing date. For applications claiming priority or disclosure exceptions, the law is applied as of the filing date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: divisional filed July 1, 2009 based on parent filed before June 30, 2009 — apply pre-revision Act; international applications use filing date of international application for law application. Use claim-by-claim reference dates where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: The search for prior art is performed during examination to discover relevant state of the art to assess patentability (e.g., novelty and inventive step), and includes searches for prior-filed applications under Articles 36 and 29(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary, examiner may outsource search to authorized prior art search institute pursuant to Article 58(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure prior to search: analysis and use of application content
rubrics_metrics.description: Before searching, the examiner shall analyze technical subject-matter of the invention; searches should be based on the claimed invention but the examiner shall pay due regard to the description and drawings if necessary. When the application cites documents, the examiner shall review them to determine whether they provide a starting point, show technology status, explain alternative solutions, or aid understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cited documents are not directly related, they may be disregarded. If necessary documents cannot be acquired by common methods, examiner shall request submission from applicant and defer examination until submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of foreign office or external search outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If foreign patent offices or search organizations have already conducted searches regarding the application, the examiner shall review their search outcomes to determine whether they can be used as relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review such external outcomes as part of examiner's assessment of prior art relevance and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search scope (databases and document types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches are carried out in systematically accessible collections/databases primarily containing patent documents of various countries, supplemented by technical journals, periodicals, books, written materials, microfiche, CD-ROM, DVD-ROM, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search strategy should determine sections of documentation to consult covering all directly relevant technical fields, and may be extended to analogous fields judged necessary in each case based on initial search outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions under which search is not required or is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: No special search effort is needed or search may be limited where: ① amendment includes new matter (Patent Act Art.47); ② the claimed invention is not patentable under Article 32; ③ the claimed invention is incomplete or not industrially applicable under Article 29; ④ claims lack unity (Article 45) such that they do not relate to one invention or a linked group forming single inventive concept; ⑤ the examiner is unable to understand the invention due to lack of written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall notify applicant if a meaningful search is impossible for some/all claims. If lack of unity, examiner may first notify lack-of-unity grounds and await applicant response. If invention can be understood despite specification deficiencies, proceed with search within that understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time coverage of search and reference dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary rule: search documents published before the filing date (or, for priority applications, before the priority date). Exceptions: in exceptional cases search may extend to documents published after filing date for purposes of applying Articles 29(3),(4) or 36. For applications with priority claims, the basic reference date for each claim is the filing date of the application, but if documents published between earliest priority date and filing date are found, examiner shall determine reference date for each claim between priority date and filing date and then decide which documents to cite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents published after filing date may be used as supporting material to confirm incorrectness/incompleteness of underlying facts. When reference dates are clear per claim, examiner may set priority date per claim and search by claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of search
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may suspend the search when prior art clearly demonstrates lack of novelty or inventive step for the entire claimed invention. Also, if completing the search would require substantial time/energy, examiner shall devise most effective method to conduct thorough search within available time/cost and may suspend search if rational judgment fails to discover effective prior arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is permitted when further search is unlikely to change outcome or is impracticable given resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles of search (equivalents, dependent claims, categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search should consider prior art incorporating technical features equivalent to claimed features in light of the description; equivalents are not limited to explicitly described technical features. Examiner conducts prior art search for dependent claims that fall within identical classification as the independent claim; dependent claims are interpreted as restricted by features of claims they depend on. When independent claim patentability is not questioned, no need to further search dependent claims. If application contains claims of different categories, all must be included in search, though if product claim is clearly novel/non-obvious, no special effort to search related process/use claims is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (e.g., welding interpreted to include gluing/riveting unless welding is essential). Examiner may search inventions stated in description but not claimed if no excessive effort required and applicant might amend to include them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of prior art documents and reliance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art shall be relied upon in grounds for rejection only if there are no doubts concerning that it was publicly known/practiced or described in a distributed publication. Counterpart documents in a language understandable to examiner may be relied on when original is in an unreadable language. Abstracts can be relied on for denying novelty/inventive step but examiner must notify grounds based on abstract only and prefer full text when obtainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of rejection must be accompanied by copies of all documents relied upon, except bulky documents (then copy relevant pages). If applicant has easy Internet access/agent or electronic filing, examiner may provide URL and publication number instead of attaching copies. If prior art is another application not yet laid open, defer examination until publication — can rely only after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification/annotation of cited prior art relevance (X, Y, A, O, P, E, T, L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related prior art in search reports can be classified by relevance: ① 'X' — alone destroys novelty or inventive step; ② 'Y' — destroys inventive step when combined with other documents; ③ 'A' — related but not X or Y; ④ 'O' — oral disclosure/use/exhibition; ⑤ 'P' — published between international filing date and priority date; ⑥ 'E' — filed before international filing date but published after it; ⑦ 'T' — discloses principle/theory or disclosed later than priority/filing date of international application; ⑧ 'L' — may throw doubt on a priority claim or negate claimed invention or determine other contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should annotate citation sheets and ER with X/Y (at least) to indicate relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures after searching: Examination Report contents and relevance indication
rubrics_metrics.description: After searching, the examiner prepares an Examination Report (ER). When identifying documents cited in the ER, the examiner should indicate the relevance of each document in the citation sheet with an X or Y annotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ER may contain keywords and search history (search DB title, search formula, number of matches). Examiner may add examination references found in the search to the ER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and handling of authorized prior art search institute outcomes (outsourced search)
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO may outsource prior-art searches to authorized prior art search institutes to mitigate examiner burden and shorten examination time, improving quality and protecting applicants' interest. Examiner selects applications per monthly schedule, head confirms and requests the institute; Information Management Division provides applications to institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions: examiner must request external search before starting examination for applications filed by current KIPO examiners, former examiners within 2 years, or applications filed by a searcher of the authorized institute supervised by KIPO; avoid requesting the institute that employs the applicant's searcher. Examiner conducts preliminary review before substantive examination and confirmation review after substantive examination to check delivery method, appropriateness of searched documents, relevancy accuracy, balanced composition, and other issues. Search outcome format is designated by KIPO (Search Report on Prior Art with comparisons, page/line references). Examiner prepares Review Statement and reports review outcomes up chain; service contracts may oblige reexamination by institute if outcomes are unutilized. Examiner prepares analysis report illustrating utility of external search outcomes in the Patent Examination Processing System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview of examination process and right to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application fails to satisfy requirements of the Patent Act, the examiner shall notify grounds for rejection and provide applicant an opportunity to submit a written argument. If argument/amendment still fails to traverse the notified grounds, examiner shall make a decision to reject the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination proceeds following prescribed flowchart/process; applicants have procedural opportunities to respond before final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of the invention for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall clearly understand claimed subject matter in light of the specification by considering the problems to be solved, means for solving the problems, what differentiates from the background art, and effects of the invention. Examination proceeds based on the specification as originally filed but should take into account amendments made by the applicant prior to notice of rejection. Claims should be construed within general scope and meaning of the technical field unless specifically defined in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Part V for confirmation methods for amended specifications; be cautious about construing claim terms beyond their logical meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of prior art documents during substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall determine whether retrieved prior art provides grounds for rejection regarding novelty, inventive step, enlarged concept of novelty or first-to-file application. Publication date is critical — examiner shall review bibliography to ascertain whether publication date precedes filing/priority date. Examiner shall have clear understanding of technical issues disclosed in prior art and be careful not to acknowledge matters not disclosed or to over-interpret claims without logical grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed guidance on publication dates and enlarged concept of novelty appears in other sections (e.g., Chapter II of Part 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special applications: formalities and procedures for priority, divisional, converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications with priority claims, disclosure exceptions, divisional or converted applications, examiner shall conduct formalities examination concerning validity of priority claims and related procedures prior to substantive examination. If priority/domestic/treaty claims or disclosure exception claims do not meet requirements, examiner shall request amendment and may invalidate the relevant procedure if deficiency is not amended. For divisional/converted applications not meeting applicant/period requirements, examiner shall provide opportunity to explain and may return application documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Part VI for detailed formalities and claim procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim under treaty: entitlement, timing, reference date rules, and evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Entitlement: priority under the treaty may be claimed by the applicant who filed in a Treaty State or legitimate successor; examiner may request evidential documents proving legitimacy. Timing: treaty priority must be claimed within 12 months from earliest filing date; if claimed after statutory period, examiner requests amendment and may invalidate if not cured. Reference dates: where invention is identical (including substantially identical) to first-country application, reference date is filing date of first-country application; for matter not described in first-country application, reference date is filing date of application claiming priority. For multiple priorities, earliest filing date of first-country applications applicable for common inventions; claim-by-claim determination of reference date is principle. Evidential documents for priority must be submitted within one year and four months from earliest filing date; failure to submit within statutory period causes loss of priority effect; post-period submission does not cure deficiency. Copies of description/drawings may be exempt if on-line exchange systems between countries are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application in first country claims priority based on an earlier application, that first-country application may not be regarded as the 'earliest application' under Paris Convention for inventions described in both; examiner should specify reasons when applying non-retroactivity in notice of grounds. Examiner should not examine whether the first-country application is pending. When evidential documents are missing, examiner requests procedural amendment and may invalidate procedure if not amended.
